query: Why do resolution duration values vary across tickets?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Category of incident plausibly affects both which agent/process handles it (treatment routing) and the resolution duration; a common cause candidate.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: The nature of the failure affects both how it is resolved (treatment) and how long it takes; plausible common cause of difficulty and handling.

per_column.name: affected_system_type
per_column.rationale: System type influences routing/assignment and inherent resolution complexity; plausible common cause.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs system-wide) affects prioritization/staffing (treatment) and duration; plausible common cause.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Whether the resolver matched (e.g., correct/appropriate resolver) is a candidate cause whose effect on duration is being attributed.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: The agent handling the ticket is a candidate cause of duration variation; a plausible treatment whose effect is attributed.

per_column.name: open_hour_of_day
per_column.rationale: Time of opening affects staffing availability (treatment/assignment) and duration; plausible common cause.

per_column.name: caller_type
per_column.rationale: Caller type may affect prioritization/assignment and duration; plausible common cause.

per_column.name: is_repeat_or_cluster_incident
per_column.rationale: Repeat/cluster status affects both handling approach and duration; plausible common cause, though could partly be a mediator.

judge.rationale: The query ('Why do resolution durations vary?') names no confounders, so all surfaced variables are genuinely derived from the data/text, satisfying the decisive test. The set supplies plausible treatments (assigned_agent, resolver_match) whose effect on duration is being attributed, and multiple candidate confounders that plausibly cause both the treatment (routing/assignment) and the outcome (duration): incident_category, failure_mode, affected_system_type, affected_scope. These are genuine common-cause candidates capturing intrinsic ticket difficulty that drives both who/how it is handled and how long it takes. Weaker items (caller_type, open_hour_of_day, is_repeat_or_cluster_incident) are plausible but partly ambiguous — is_repeat_or_cluster_incident in particular risks being a mediator/collider. Overall the columns do set up a causal estimation with treatment plus non-copied confounders, hence moderate-to-good confounder quality.
